If you want Google to show your business when someone nearby searches "electrician near me," open your Google Business Profile tonight and check:

Primary category is your main trade
Service area lists the towns you actually drive to
Real job photos, added every week
drafts.pattern: Conditional 'If you want X...' benefit hook plus a short checklist (alexgroberman's top post of the month, 76,971 views)
drafts.video_tip: Screen-record 15 seconds on a phone: open a Google Business Profile, tap Edit, and point to the category and service area fields. Vertical video, no voiceover needed.
drafts.best_time_ct: Weekday 8-11 AM CT (weak signal: the six focus accounts' posts in that window ran 1.08x their own median views, n=24. Correlation only, and he has no history of his own yet.)
drafts.link_reply: Optional reply: 'If you want a second set of eyes on yours, I do this for trades businesses: [StableAFdesigns link]'

drafts.text:
Pull up your own website on your phone right now.

Can you tap your phone number without scrolling?

If not, fix that first. Someone with water on the floor isn't going to dig through your menu. They'll call the next plumber on the list.

Number at the top. Tap to call.
drafts.pattern: Imperative challenge to the reader, then the consequence (sweatystartup 'Call around for home service companies...', 66,339 views, text only)
drafts.video_tip: Film your thumb on a phone loading a contractor site where the number is buried (blur the name), then one where it's tappable up top. Two 5-second clips side by side are enough.
drafts.best_time_ct: Weekday 8-11 AM CT (weak signal: the six focus accounts' posts in that window ran 1.08x their own median views, n=24. Correlation only, and he has no history of his own yet.)
drafts.link_reply: Optional reply: 'More fixes like this, written for trades: [StableAFdesigns link]'

drafts.text:
Contractors will pay for a full truck wrap and yard signs, then send people to a website built in 2014.

The truck says pro. The website says maybe they'll call back.

It's ok to be a small shop. Just don't look like one online.
drafts.pattern: Spend-mismatch opinion that ends on a short punchline (mhp_guy 'I can't imagine spending only $1k on what your POTENTIAL customers see... It's ok to BE mom & pop. Just don't LOOK mom & pop!', 130,647 views)
drafts.video_tip: Shoot a photo of a wrapped work truck (your sister's, or one you have permission to show) next to a phone showing an old-looking site. One image that shows the gap does the work.
drafts.best_time_ct: Weekday 8-11 AM CT (weak signal: the six focus accounts' posts in that window ran 1.08x their own median views, n=24. Correlation only, and he has no history of his own yet.)
drafts.link_reply: none (let it stand on its own)

drafts.text:
GFCI vs AFCI ⚡

GFCI trips when current leaks to ground, like through a person. That's why they go near water: kitchens, baths, garages, outdoors.

AFCI trips when it detects arcing in the wiring, a common cause of house fires.

Where each is required depends on local code.
drafts.pattern: Two-thing contrast headline with emoji, then a plain answer (electric_4u 'Voltage ≠ Current ⚡', its best post in the sample at 11,642 views)
drafts.video_tip: Close-up photo of a GFCI outlet next to an AFCI breaker in a panel, labeled with two words each. Or a 5-second clip pressing TEST on a GFCI so it clicks off.
drafts.best_time_ct: no data yet (electric_4u posts at scattered times, 2 AM to 1 PM CT, with no clear pattern)

drafts.text:
Panel upgrade today in [city].

Old: [real detail, e.g. age/brand/amperage of the old panel]
New: [real detail of the new panel]

[photo of the old panel] [photo of the finished panel]

[One line from her about what she noticed on this job, in her words]
drafts.pattern: Plain 'working on...' show-the-work post with the photo carrying it (DannPetty 'Working on my portfolio.', 28,721 views)
drafts.video_tip: Shoot the before and after from the same spot and angle, panel cover off, good light. A 3-second pan across the labeled breakers at the end helps too.
drafts.best_time_ct: no data yet (electric_4u posts at scattered times, 2 AM to 1 PM CT, with no clear pattern)

drafts.text:
Myth: if a breaker keeps tripping, the breaker is bad.

Usually it's doing its job. Something on that circuit is overloaded or faulty, and the breaker cuts power before the wire overheats.

Never swap in a bigger breaker to make it stop. Have an electrician find the cause.
drafts.pattern: Correct a common belief about what a breaker does, in one short answer (electric_4u 'Ever wondered what a circuit breaker actually does? 🔌', 7,927 views)
drafts.video_tip: A 10-second clip of your sister pointing at a breaker and saying the myth line to camera, then the fix. Face plus panel builds trust faster than a graphic.
drafts.best_time_ct: no data yet (electric_4u posts at scattered times, 2 AM to 1 PM CT, with no clear pattern)
